findings.description: publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public IP/endpoint, exposing the database listener to the internet. Although the attached security group only permits 3306 from the VPC CIDR, the instance is directly addressable from outside the VPC, defeating network segmentation.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS instance's data, automated backups, and snapshots unencrypted at rest, so anyone with access to the underlying storage or a snapshot can read the data.

The database master password (var.password), username, endpoint, and database name are interpolated into the EC2 user_data script, which writes them in cleartext to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc on the web server. The secret is embedded in the instance user data (retrievable via instance metadata) and stored in plaintext on disk, exposing the database credentials.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*" to a role assumed by an EC2 instance. This is effectively full administrative access to three services, allowing privilege escalation, data exfiltration, and resource destruction from a compromised web server.

The EC2 instance is associated with the catalog_app_profile instance profile, whose role carries the wildcard s3/ec2/rds policy. A compromise of the public-facing PHP application — which already leaks DB credentials — directly yields broad cloud API access.
